patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Wrike documents a broader use-case set; VektorOS is narrower/specialist.

Wrike documents a broader use-case set; VektorOS is narrower/specialist. Choose VektorOS only if your buying job matches “Business and operations software — affiliate partner in project management.” rather than Wrike's shape. Choose Wrike only if your buying job matches “Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team from $10/use” rather than VektorOS's shape. Workflow advantage: VektorOS leans shared coverage; Wrike leans project-tracking, resource-planning. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Wrike documents a broader use-case set; VektorOS is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: VektorOS is Business and operations software — affiliate partner in project management.; Wrike is Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team from $10/user/mo annual..
- Company-size focus: VektorOS (small-business, mid-market) vs Wrike (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: VektorOS-leaning — vs Wrike-leaning project-tracking, resource-planning, team-collaboration-work.
- Researched limits: VektorOS — SMB ops platform — limited public pricing transparency; Wrike — Business tier pricing jump.

Limitations — VektorOS: SMB ops platform — limited public pricing transparency; Wrike: Business tier pricing jump; Heavier admin than lightweight tools.

Poor-fit cases: VektorOS is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SMB ops platform — limited public pricing transparency · Wrike is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Business tier pricing jump · Avoid VektorOS if you actually need Wrike's motion (Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team fr)
